FOR campaign/the-coherence -- THE CONTAINER WORKED. It built, installed the pinned Mesa, and compiled inside itself. It died on git, not on rendering, and there are TWO blockers rather than one. e146f9c2567a, rc=11 at clients after 2096 s; gate rc=0 for the third run.

HOW FAR IT GOT, which is nearly all the way:

  #1..#4  Containerfile loaded, base image resolved by digest, cached
  #5      apt-get update, all three pinned versions asserted and installed
  then    cargo compiled hornvale-* and planetarium INSIDE the container at
          /workspace

WHERE IT STOPPED:

  error: failed to run custom build command for `planetarium`
  thread 'main' panicked at planetarium/build.rs:14:9: git build provenance failed

build.rs runs `git -C <manifest>/../../.. rev-parse HEAD` and `git status
--porcelain`, and asserts both succeed. Inside the container that root is
/workspace.

I REPRODUCED BOTH FAILURES WITH THE IMAGE YOUR CONTAINERFILE PINS, so this is
measured rather than reasoned:

  mount = the chamber's worktree (what actually happens):
    fatal: not a git repository:
    /home/nathan/Projects/hornvale/.git/worktrees/hornvale-sluice-wt

  mount = a normal checkout (the control):
    fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at '/workspace'

TWO SEPARATE THINGS, and fixing only the first leaves you red:

  1. THE CHAMBER RUNS IN A LINKED WORKTREE. Its `.git` is a FILE reading
     "gitdir: /home/nathan/Projects/hornvale/.git/worktrees/hornvale-sluice-wt",
     which points outside your `-v "$root:/workspace:ro"` mount, so there is no
     repository in there at all. A developer's own checkout has `.git` as a real
     directory, which is why this passes for you and cannot pass in the chamber.

  2. EVEN WITH THE GITDIR MOUNTED, git refuses on ownership: the container runs
     as root over a bind mount owned by uid 1000. That is the control arm above.

WHAT I WOULD DO -- TAKE GIT OUT OF THE CONTAINER ENTIRELY. Compute the
provenance OUTSIDE, where the repository is real and owned by you, and pass it
in:

  docker run ... -e PLANETARIUM_BUILD_REVISION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" \
                 -e PLANETARIUM_BUILD_CLEAN="$(git status --porcelain | head -c1 | wc -c)"

and have build.rs prefer those when set, falling back to running git when they
are absent. build.rs already emits exactly these two as
`cargo:rustc-env=PLANETARIUM_BUILD_*`, so the shape is unchanged -- you would
only be letting the caller supply what it already computes.

That is robust to all three things that bit here: linked worktrees, uid
mismatch, and a read-only mount. Mounting the gitdir plus a safe.directory
exception would also work and needs two host-specific paths baked into a
script, which is the undeclared-host-state pattern we have been trying to keep
out of the gate.

YOUR GATE HAS BEEN GREEN FOR THREE RUNS and the driver problem is genuinely
solved -- no SIGSEGV, no 35-minute render, the pinned image does what the A/B
said it would. This is the last thing and it is not a rendering problem.
